  "run_id": "347e4c36d5de",
  "round": 4,
  "topic": "direct empirical studies of proposition-level partial reply scope in workplace email or enterprise dialogue, especially multi-question messages, unanswered subquestions, scoped approval/rejection, and responses linked jointly to multiple antecedent propositions",
  "gaps": [
    {
      "id": "gap-1",
      "description": "Direct empirical evidence is still missing for proposition-level agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, and answer scope in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat, especially short responses applying to only part of a preceding message. Existing workplace-email studies primarily cover question-answer linkage, while proposition-sensitive acceptance/rejection evidence comes from broader dialogue work.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"partial reply\" OR \"response scope\" email workplace dialogue proposition agreement rejection approval",
      "resolution_notes": "The available corpus does not directly validate exact partial agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, and answer scope together in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat. Resolving this gap requires additional empirical studies or datasets containing proposition-level reply-scope annotations in real workplace communication."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-2",
      "description": "A validated combined msgloom annotation and evaluation scheme is still missing for exact proposition/span targets with exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, discontinuous, multiple-antecedent, composite, and explicit no-link outcomes. The literature validates many ingredients separately but not the combined workplace contract.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "This can be resolved without additional papers by specifying the combined annotation contract, producing a representative workplace annotation set, running independent multi-annotator labeling, measuring agreement separately for target spans and relation categories, adjudicating disagreements, and benchmarking evaluation metrics for exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, discontinuous, multiple-antecedent, composite, and no-link outcomes. Validation should include held-out examples and error analysis to determine whether the contract is reproducible and operationally useful."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-3",
      "description": "Direct evidence for multi-question partial replies is materially stronger, including email cases where only a subset of questions is answered and answer sentences can map to several questions, but the corpus still does not fully validate proposition-level handling of mixed workplace questions, requests, and alternatives together or a complete unresolved-subquestion detector.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"multiple questions\" \"partial answer\" dialogue email question answer alignment unanswered subquestions",
      "resolution_notes": "Existing evidence narrows the gap by demonstrating incomplete replies, unanswered questions, and one-to-many question-answer mappings, but does not establish the broader proposition-level behavior required for messages mixing questions, requests, and alternatives. Additional empirical workplace studies are needed, particularly datasets that explicitly annotate resolved versus unresolved subquestions and other proposition types."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-4",
      "description": "It remains open how authentic workplace systems should distinguish one response independently targeting several antecedent propositions from one response targeting a single composite multi-proposition discourse object. Both structures are supported in dialogue and abstract-reference research, but direct workplace evaluation of this distinction is missing.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "MEDIUM",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"multi-antecedent\" dialogue response \"composite antecedent\" proposition discourse email",
      "resolution_notes": "The corpus supports multi-parent response links and composite discourse antecedents separately, but does not directly test whether annotators or systems can reliably distinguish independent multiple targets from a single composite antecedent in authentic workplace communication. Resolving this requires additional empirical evidence with explicit annotations for both structures."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-5",
      "description": "The msgloom policy for abstention, ambiguity, missing antecedents, and asymmetric error costs remains unvalidated. Explicit no-link, ambiguous alternatives, future-context dependence, and partial-credit scoring are supported, but no paper establishes thresholds appropriate to the product cost of inventing an approval or commitment versus leaving a link unresolved.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "This is a product-specific decision problem that should be resolved through benchmark construction and cost-sensitive evaluation rather than further literature search. Define operational false-link and missed-link costs, build a validation set containing approval, rejection, commitment, ambiguity, missing-antecedent, and no-link cases, calibrate model confidence, sweep abstention thresholds, and evaluate precision, recall, calibration, selective risk, and expected cost. Thresholds can then be chosen separately for high-risk relations such as approvals or commitments and lower-risk informational links."
    }
  ],

    "should_continue": false,

  }
}
